checks.diagnosis: The prompt treats cuts before a forthcoming verb or essential complement as acceptable, underestimating how leaving a pre-cut fragment without its predicate makes the fragment contradictory or meaningless.
checks.evidence: cmn_hans_cn_324, cmn_hans_cn_223, cmn_hans_cn_543 — each shows the policy kept a cut immediately before the clause's main verb/complement (those single cuts had very high contradiction), and the target moves the cut later so the predicate is not split.
checks.type_predicate: Markers that fall immediately before a lexical verb or essential clausal complement when the text before the marker contains no main predicate (i.e., the pre-cut stretch is a nominal/modifier fragment lacking the clause's verb).

edit.text: Do not cut immediately before the main verb or an essential complement when the preceding segment contains no predicate; treat such positions as must-not-cut (move cuts later to keep predicate+arguments together).

orders.diagnosis: The prompt prefers interior splits inside tight multiword units (verb–object, '…的…' modifiers, foreign names, numeral+measure), rather than preferring cuts that keep those units intact.
orders.evidence: cmn_hans_cn_372, cmn_hans_cn_1346 — in both, the policy ranks a cut that splits a tight verb‑object or multi‑character unit above a later cut that preserves the unit; the measurement prefers the latter.
orders.type_predicate: Sentences in which two candidate markers occur in the same clause and one marker lies inside a contiguous multi-character unit (verb+object, a '…的…' modifier, foreign‑script or Romanized name, or numeral+measure) while the other marker immediately follows that unit.

edit.text: When one candidate splits a tight multi-character unit (verb–object, a '…的…' modifier, foreign name, or numeral+measure) and another candidate immediately follows that unit, prefer the latter marker that keeps the unit intact.
